fields.label: Locale
fields.desc: The locale used for Sunshine's user interface.

fields.label: Sunshine Name
fields.desc: The name displayed by Moonlight. If not specified, the PC's hostname is used

fields.label: Log Level
fields.desc: The minimum log level printed to standard out

fields.label: Command Preparations
fields.desc: Configure a list of commands to be executed before or after running any application. If any of the specified preparation commands fail, the application launch process will be aborted.

fields.label: PreRelease Notifications
fields.desc: Whether to be notified of new pre-release versions of Sunshine

fields.label: Enable system tray
fields.desc: Show icon in system tray and display desktop notifications

fields.label: Enable Gamepad Input
fields.desc: Allows guests to control the host system with a gamepad / controller

fields.label: Gamepad Backend
fields.desc: Choose which Windows gamepad backend Sunshine may use. All Available Drivers prefers Virtual HID Broker when licensed and falls back to ViGEmBus. Virtual HID Broker is an optional paid upgrade. ViGEmBus supports only Xbox 360 and DualShock 4, has limited features, and has reached end of life. None disables gamepads and broker notices without affecting keyboard or mouse input.

fields.label: Emulated Gamepad Type
fields.desc: Choose which type of gamepad to emulate on the host

fields.label: Map Back/Select to Touchpad Click
fields.desc: When using PlayStation-style gamepad emulation, map Back/Select to Touchpad Click

fields.label: Emulate a PlayStation-style gamepad if the client gamepad reports motion sensors are present
fields.desc: If disabled, motion sensors will not be taken into account during gamepad type selection.

fields.label: Emulate a PlayStation-style gamepad if the client gamepad reports a touchpad is present
fields.desc: If disabled, touchpad presence will not be taken into account during gamepad type selection.

fields.label: Randomize virtual controller MAC
fields.desc: Use a random MAC address for PlayStation-style virtual controllers instead of one based on the controller index. This avoids mixing per-controller settings when controllers are swapped on the client.

fields.label: Home/Guide Button Emulation Timeout
fields.desc: If the Back/Select button is held down for the specified number of milliseconds, a Home/Guide button press is emulated. If set to a value < 0 (default), holding the Back/Select button will not emulate the Home/Guide button.

fields.label: Enable Keyboard Input
fields.desc: Allows guests to control the host system with the keyboard

fields.label: Key Repeat Delay
fields.desc: Control how fast keys will repeat themselves. The initial delay in milliseconds before repeating keys.

fields.label: Key Repeat Frequency
fields.desc: How often keys repeat every second. This configurable option supports decimals.

fields.label: Always Send Scancodes
fields.desc: Sending scancodes enhances compatibility with games and apps but may result in incorrect keyboard input from certain clients that aren't using a US English keyboard layout. Enable if keyboard input is not working at all in certain applications. Disable if keys on the client are generating the wrong input on the host.

fields.label: Map Right Alt key to Windows key
fields.desc: It may be possible that you cannot send the Windows Key from Moonlight directly. In those cases it may be useful to make Sunshine think the Right Alt key is the Windows key

fields.label: Enable Mouse Input
fields.desc: Allows guests to control the host system with the mouse

fields.label: High Resolution Scrolling Support
fields.desc: When enabled, Sunshine will pass through high resolution scroll events from Moonlight clients. This can be useful to disable for older applications that scroll too fast with high resolution scroll events.

fields.label: Native Pen/Touch Support
fields.desc: When enabled, Sunshine will pass through native pen/touch events from Moonlight clients. This can be useful to disable for older applications without native pen/touch support.

fields.label: Keybindings
fields.desc: Remap Windows virtual-key codes received from Moonlight. Each row maps a source code to the code Sunshine sends to the host. Choose from the complete list of Microsoft-defined virtual-key codes. Incomplete or invalid rows are not saved.

fields.label: Virtual Sink
fields.desc: Manually specify a virtual audio device to use. If unset, the device is chosen automatically. We strongly recommend leaving this field blank to use automatic device selection!

fields.label: Stream Audio
fields.desc: Whether to stream audio or not. Disabling this can be useful for streaming headless displays as second monitors.

fields.label: Install Steam Audio Drivers
fields.desc: If Steam is installed, this will automatically install the Steam Streaming Speakers driver to support 5.1/7.1 surround sound and muting host audio.

fields.label: Externally Managed Audio
fields.desc: Capture only the configured Audio Sink without changing Windows defaults or device formats. Requires an explicit Audio Sink. Virtual Sink selection, automatic Steam audio driver installation, and Moonlight's host-playback toggle are ignored; manage playback and application routing in your audio mixer.

options.label: Use resolution provided by the client (default)
Use FPS value provided by the client (default)
Switch on/off the HDR mode as requested by the client (default)

fields.label: Config revert delay
fields.desc: Additional delay in milliseconds to wait before reverting configuration when the app has been closed or the last session terminated. Main purpose is to provide a smoother transition when quickly switching between apps.

fields.label: Config revert on disconnect
fields.desc: Revert configuration upon disconnect of all clients instead of app close or last session termination.

fields.label: Maximum Bitrate
fields.desc: The maximum bitrate (in Kbps) that Sunshine will encode the stream at. If set to 0, it will always use the bitrate requested by Moonlight.

fields.label: Minimum FPS Target
fields.desc: The lowest effective FPS a stream can reach. A value of 0 is treated as roughly half of the stream's FPS. A setting of 20 is recommended if you stream 24 or 30fps content.

fields.label: UPnP
fields.desc: Automatically configure port forwarding for streaming over the Internet

fields.label: Address Family
fields.desc: Set the address family used by Sunshine

fields.label: Bind address
fields.desc: Set an IP address that exists on this host. An IPv4 address works with either address-family mode; an IPv6 address requires dual-stack mode. If left blank, Sunshine will bind to all available addresses for the configured address family.

fields.label: Port
fields.desc: Set the family of ports used by Sunshine

fields.label: Origin Web UI Allowed
fields.desc: The origin of the remote endpoint address that is not denied access to Web UI

options.label: Only localhost may access Web UI
Only those in LAN may access Web UI

fields.label: CSRF Allowed Origins
fields.desc: Comma-separated list of additional allowed origins for CSRF protection (appended to defaults: localhost variants and web UI port). Only add origins you trust. Each origin must include protocol and host (e.g., https://example.com).

fields.label: External IP
fields.desc: If no external IP address is given, Sunshine will automatically detect external IP

fields.label: LAN Encryption Mode
fields.desc: This determines when encryption will be used when streaming over your local network. Encryption can reduce streaming performance, particularly on less powerful hosts and clients.

fields.label: WAN Encryption Mode
fields.desc: This determines when encryption will be used when streaming over the Internet. Encryption can reduce streaming performance, particularly on less powerful hosts and clients.

fields.label: Ping Timeout
fields.desc: How long to wait in milliseconds for data from moonlight before shutting down the stream

fields.label: Packet Size Limit
fields.desc: Limit the packet size to avoid fragmentation on a low MTU link. This helps reduce packet loss and micro-stuttering, while streaming over a layer 2 VPN to clients that cannot configure this value, e.g. Moonlight for Android/iOS. Reduce the bitrate when using low values. Values larger than 1456 require jumbo frames. Range: 0, 200-65535. A value of 0 will disable the limit.

fields.label: Apps File
fields.desc: The file where current apps of Sunshine are stored.

fields.label: Credentials File
fields.desc: Store Username/Password separately from Sunshine's state file.

fields.label: Logfile Path
fields.desc: The file where the current Sunshine log is stored. At startup, up to five previous logs are retained with .1 through .5 suffixes.

fields.label: Private Key
fields.desc: The private key used for the web UI and Moonlight client pairing. For best compatibility, this should be an RSA-2048 private key.

fields.label: Certificate
fields.desc: The certificate used for the web UI and Moonlight client pairing. For best compatibility, this should have an RSA-2048 public key.

fields.label: State File
fields.desc: The file where current state of Sunshine is stored

fields.label: FEC Percentage
fields.desc: Percentage of error correcting packets per data packet in each video frame. Set to 0 to disable forward error correction. Higher values can correct for more network packet loss, but at the cost of increasing bandwidth usage.

fields.label: Quantization Parameter
fields.desc: Some devices may not support Constant Bit Rate. For those devices, QP is used instead. Higher value means more compression, but less quality.

fields.label: Minimum CPU Thread Count
fields.desc: Increasing the value slightly reduces encoding efficiency, but the tradeoff is usually worth it to gain the use of more CPU cores for encoding. The ideal value is the lowest value that can reliably encode at your desired streaming settings on your hardware.

fields.label: HEVC Support
fields.desc: Allows the client to request HEVC Main or HEVC Main10 video streams. HEVC is more CPU-intensive to encode, so enabling this may reduce performance when using software encoding.

options.label: Sunshine will advertise support for HEVC based on encoder capabilities (recommended)
Sunshine will not advertise support for HEVC
Sunshine will advertise support for HEVC Main profile
Sunshine will advertise support for HEVC Main and Main10 (HDR) profiles

fields.label: AV1 Support
fields.desc: Allows the client to request AV1 Main 8-bit or 10-bit video streams. AV1 is more CPU-intensive to encode, so enabling this may reduce performance when using software encoding.

options.label: Sunshine will advertise support for AV1 based on encoder capabilities (recommended)
Sunshine will not advertise support for AV1
Sunshine will advertise support for AV1 Main 8-bit profile
Sunshine will advertise support for AV1 Main 8-bit and 10-bit (HDR) profiles

fields.label: Force a Specific Capture Method
fields.desc: On automatic mode Sunshine will use the first one that works. NvFBC requires patched nvidia drivers.

fields.label: Treat FP16 SDR captures as gamma-encoded
fields.desc: Enable this if the stream looks washed out or its highlights are blown out while the display is in SDR mode and the desktop is captured in FP16 format (the log shows DXGI_FORMAT_R16G16B16A16_FLOAT as the desktop format). Sunshine will then skip the sRGB curve for FP16 SDR captures. Leave this disabled otherwise, because it darkens the stream when the FP16 capture is linear. It has no effect when the display is in HDR mode.

fields.label: Force a Specific Encoder
fields.desc: Force a specific encoder, otherwise Sunshine will select the best available option. Note: If you specify a hardware encoder on Windows, it must match the GPU where the display is connected.

fields.label: Performance preset
fields.desc: Higher numbers improve compression (quality at given bitrate) at the cost of increased encoding latency. Recommended to change only when limited by network or decoder, otherwise similar effect can be accomplished by increasing bitrate.

fields.label: Two-pass mode
fields.desc: Adds preliminary encoding pass. This allows to detect more motion vectors, better distribute bitrate across the frame and more strictly adhere to bitrate limits. Disabling it is not recommended since this can lead to occasional bitrate overshoot and subsequent packet loss.

fields.label: Spatial AQ
fields.desc: Assign higher QP values to flat regions of the video. Recommended to enable when streaming at lower bitrates.

fields.label: Single-frame VBV/HRD percentage increase
fields.desc: By default sunshine uses single-frame VBV/HRD, which means any encoded video frame size is not expected to exceed requested bitrate divided by requested frame rate. Relaxing this restriction can be beneficial and act as low-latency variable bitrate, but may also lead to packet loss if the network doesn't have buffer headroom to handle bitrate spikes. Maximum accepted value is 400, which corresponds to 5x increased encoded video frame upper size limit.

fields.label: Use realtime priority in hardware accelerated gpu scheduling
fields.desc: Currently NVIDIA drivers may freeze in encoder when HAGS is enabled, realtime priority is used and VRAM utilization is close to maximum. Disabling this option lowers the priority to high, sidestepping the freeze at the cost of reduced capture performance when the GPU is heavily loaded.

fields.label: Split frame encoding
fields.desc: Split the encoding of each video frame over multiple NVENC hardware units. Significantly reduces host processing latency with a marginal compression efficiency penalty. The default option enables SFE if the following conditions are met: there are 2+ NVENC units, the stream is 4K resolution or higher, and the preset is P1-P4. Set this to Enabled to use SFE at lower resolutions or higher presets.

fields.label: Prefer lower encoding latency over power savings
fields.desc: Sunshine requests maximum GPU clock speed while streaming to reduce encoding latency. Disabling it is not recommended since this can lead to significantly increased encoding latency.

fields.label: Present OpenGL/Vulkan on top of DXGI
fields.desc: Sunshine can't capture fullscreen OpenGL and Vulkan programs at full frame rate unless they present on top of DXGI. This is system-wide setting that is reverted on sunshine program exit.

fields.label: Prefer CAVLC over CABAC in H.264
fields.desc: Simpler form of entropy coding. CAVLC needs around 10% more bitrate for same quality. Only relevant for really old decoding devices.

options.label: cabac -- context adaptive binary arithmetic coding - higher quality
cavlc -- context adaptive variable-length coding - faster decode

fields.label: Allow Slow HEVC Encoding
fields.desc: This can enable HEVC encoding on older Intel GPUs, at the cost of higher GPU usage and worse performance.

fields.label: AMF Usage
fields.desc: This sets the base encoding profile. All options presented below will override a subset of the usage profile, but there are additional hidden settings applied that cannot be configured elsewhere.

fields.label: AMF Rate Control
fields.desc: This controls the rate control method to ensure we are not exceeding the client bitrate target. 'cqp' is not suitable for bitrate targeting, and other options besides 'vbr_latency' depend on HRD Enforcement to help constrain bitrate overflows.

options.label: cbr -- constant bitrate (recommended if HRD is enabled)
vbr_latency -- latency constrained variable bitrate (recommended if HRD is disabled; default)

fields.label: AMF Hypothetical Reference Decoder (HRD) Enforcement
fields.desc: Increases the constraints on rate control to meet HRD model requirements. This greatly reduces bitrate overflows, but may cause encoding artifacts or reduced quality on certain cards.

fields.label: AMF Max AU Size (bits)
fields.desc: Maximum encoded H.264 or HEVC Access Unit size in bits. Empty or -1 leaves the AMF default. Use only to cap oversized frames that exceed Sunshine's FEC capacity. The limit depends on packet size and FEC percentage, not bitrate or frame rate. See the documentation for sizing.

fields.label: AMF Quality
fields.desc: This controls the balance between encoding speed and quality.

fields.label: AMF Preanalysis
fields.desc: This enables rate-control preanalysis, which may increase quality at the expense of increased encoding latency.

fields.label: AMF Variance Based Adaptive Quantization (VBAQ)
fields.desc: The human visual system is typically less sensitive to artifacts in highly textured areas. In VBAQ mode, pixel variance is used to indicate the complexity of spatial textures, allowing the encoder to allocate more bits to smoother areas. Enabling this feature leads to improvements in subjective visual quality with some content.

fields.label: AMF Coder (H264)
fields.desc: Allows you to select the entropy encoding to prioritize quality or encoding speed. H.264 only.

options.label: cabac -- context adaptive binary arithmetic coding - higher quality
cavlc -- context adaptive variable-length coding - faster decode
cabac -- context adaptive binary arithmetic coding - higher quality
cavlc -- context adaptive variable-length coding - faster decode

fields.label: Block level based bitrate control (BLBRC)
fields.desc: Enable block level rate control, which assigns different bitrate block by block. Can be combined with CBR/VBR-type rate control methods on supported encoders.

fields.label: VA-API Quality
fields.desc: Determines encoder tradeoff between quality and speed/power consumption.

fields.label: VA-API Rate Control
fields.desc: This controls the rate control method to ensure we are not exceeding the client bitrate target. Note that supported rate control methods varies by vendor, and automatic may force-enable strict bitrate enforcement on certain devices.

fields.label: Strictly enforce frame bitrate limits for H.264/HEVC on AMD GPUs
fields.desc: Enabling this option can avoid dropped frames over the network during scene changes, but video quality may be reduced during motion.

fields.label: Tuning
fields.desc: Low latency modes reduce encoding delay at the cost of quality.

fields.label: Rate Control
fields.desc: Rate control mode for encoding. Auto lets the driver decide.

fields.label: Quality
fields.desc: Determines encoder tradeoff between quality and speed.

fields.label: SW Presets
fields.desc: Optimize the trade-off between encoding speed (encoded frames per second) and compression efficiency (quality per bit in the bitstream). Defaults to superfast.

fields.label: SW Tune
fields.desc: Tuning options, which are applied after the preset. Defaults to zerolatency.

options.label: film -- use for high quality movie content; lowers deblocking
animation -- good for cartoons; uses higher deblocking and more reference frames
grain -- preserves the grain structure in old, grainy film material
fastdecode -- allows faster decoding by disabling certain filters
zerolatency -- good for fast encoding and low-latency streaming (default)
